hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement needs `NeZero N` to elaborate. In Mathlib, `gammaSet N r a` and `eisensteinSeries a k` (EisensteinSeries/Defs.lean) are defined for every `N`, and `cst` is too. The proof only uses `NeZero` in the step `ModularGroup_T_zpow_mem_verticalStrip z (NeZero.pos N)`, which moves a point into the vertical strip, and that step fails only when N = 0. So the theorem can be proved by splitting on whether N = 0. If N ≠ 0, we get the instance and the existing proof applies. If N = 0, then `ZMod 0 = ℤ` and the cast ℤ → ZMod 0 is the identity, so `gammaSet 0 1 a = {v | v = a ∧ gcd (v 0) (v 1) = 1}`. This set is `{a}` if a is coprime and empty otherwise. Since it has at most one element, `eisensteinSeries a k z` equals `eisSummand k a z` or `0`, and the limit can be checked case by case. (1) a is not coprime: the series is 0. Also a ≠ ![0,±1] because those vectors are coprime, so `cst k a = 0`. (2) a 0 ≠ 0 and a is coprime: the series is `eisSummand k a z`, which tends to `lim k a = 0` by the file's `tendsto_eisSummand hk` (it has no NeZero). Also a ≠ ![0,±1], so `cst k a = 0`. (3) a 0 = 0 and a is coprime: then |a 1| = 1, so a = ![0,1] (constant value 1 = cst) or a = ![0,-1] (constant value (-1)^(-k) = cst). In all three cases the limit is `cst k a`. Equivalently, for N = 0, take the finite sum over the subsingleton `gammaSet` of `tendsto_eisSummand`, and the resulting sum of `lim` values is `cst k a`; the proof of `tsum_lim` only uses `mem_gammaSet_iff_of_apply_zero`, which has no `NeZero`. So the theorem stays true and provable without `[NeZero N]`.
